newsitem.title: CANADA: Ottawa studies idea of Canada grain delay probe.
newsitem.headline: Ottawa studies idea of Canada grain delay probe.

text.p: Transport Minister David Anderson welcomes the call by three provinces for a federal inquiry into delayed grain shipments to Pacific ports, a spokesman for Anderson said on Tuesday.
"We welcome the idea put forward today and we'll be looking at it seriously along with a number of other ideas," said spokesman Brian Bohunicky.
But he added: "That's one idea. There are others. We'll be looking at them."
Bohunicky was unable to say whether Anderson would agree to the request.

Transport ministers of British Columbia, Saskatchewan and Manitoba on Tuesday called on Anderson "to get to the bottom of this issue" and identify the causes for the failure in the system so that similar crises are avoided in the future.
Heavy snow, extreme cold and equipment failure have led to delays in rail shipments to Pacific ports since early January, costing Prairie farmers money.
Bohunicky said Anderson's officials have been in constant contact with the various groups involved and he was very interested in looking at the backlog over the short term and the long term.
"Can we solve it this moment? No," he said.
Bohunicky said there has been some improvement in that the number of grain vessels waiting on Canada's West Coast has been reduced to 34.
